messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: SRE oncall Maya paged for INC-2026-72 - High CUDA OOM rate on serving-runtime (us-west1). Service: redwood-serving-prod. Symptom: streaming requests dropping mid-response, container restarts, node flaps. See incident dashboard: <https://internal/redwood/incidents/INC-2026-72>

Maya (oncall): I'm on it. initial telemetry shows a spike in streaming sessions with sustained token generation. GPU memory climbed until containers OOM'd and kube evicted pods.

Jared (eng-sre): Confirmed. I'm seeing repeated kernel errors in logs right before container exit: `E/CUDA: out of memory` then `abort()` in decode loop. Correlation id list: cid=3f2a.., 9b7c.., etc.

Priya (eng-runtime): Do we have client-side max_tokens values for those requests? Any runaway generation?

Maya (oncall): Good question — pulling request traces now.

Jared (eng-sre): Traces show a cluster of requests from a single API key with `max_tokens: 100000` and `stream: true`. The runtime's streaming path doesn't enforce a hard upper bound today for hosted customers.

Carlos (customer-success): I'm seeing customer reports of partial streams and retries. Likely impacting ~12 paying customers intermittently. One message from AcmeInc: "responses cutting out mid-sentence, then 500s".

Maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation we should consider: 1) blacklist offending API key 2) set route-level hard cap for streaming to 2048 tokens 3) temporarily disable streaming on the affected pool 4) scale up/cordon nodes to reduce churn. Thoughts?

Jared (eng-sre): Agree with that order. I'll blacklist the API key first to stop additional requests.

Priya (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a hotfix to enforce a `max_tokens` upper bound in the streaming handler and a fail-safe in the decode loop to drop long-running generations. Can we patch route config for hosted before code?

Maya (oncall): Let's do both in parallel. Jared: please blacklist. Priya: patch route config to hard cap.

Jared (eng-sre): Executing blacklist now.

deploy-bot: @jared started run: `redwoodctl keys revoke --key-id = ak_live_0a1b2c` (run id run-8842)

Jared (eng-sre): Blacklist applied. Observed immediate drop-off in new high-token streams. Error rate trending down but some pods still OOM from already-running sessions.

Priya (eng-runtime): Pushing a config override to set `stream_max_tokens: 2048` for prod-route using redeploy config. Command:

```
redwoodctl routes update --route-id prod-stream --set stream_max_tokens=2048 --env production
```

Priya (eng-runtime): Override applied, rolling restart only for proxy layer to pick up config, should not kill in-flight decode loops.

Maya (oncall): To stop already-running sessions causing OOMs, recommend toggling streaming off on the affected GPU pool and migrating new requests to warm standby pool. Jared, can you cordon the worst nodes and force new pods to schedule elsewhere?

Jared (eng-sre): Doing cordon/evict for nodes: gpu-usw1-a{03,07}.

```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-usw1-a03
kubectl cordon node/gpu-usw1-a07
kubectl drain node/gpu-usw1-a03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
kubectl drain node/gpu-usw1-a07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```

Jared (eng-sre): Also killing a few stuck pods to free GPU memory on the pool: `kubectl delete pod serving-rt-ff9b -n prod` etc.

Priya (eng-runtime): After the cordon and config cap, memory pressure reduced on the pool. New pods are coming up on standby pool with smaller arena sizes.

Carlos (customer-success): I've messaged affected customers with an interim note: we found a spike causing partial responses and have applied mitigations; full postmortem forthcoming. A few asked for ETA to resume normal service.

Maya (oncall): ETA: we expect full recovery in ~15-30m after the in-flight sessions drain. I'll keep channel updated.

(15m later)

Jared (eng-sre): Metrics: GPU mem usage back to baseline, OOM events dropped to zero, success rate for streaming up from 78% to 99%. Node flapping stopped.

Priya (eng-runtime): Hotfix PR ready to enforce hard cap + defensive check in decode loop: PR #3456. Patch includes: 1) global `STREAM_MAX_TOKENS = 2048` default 2) runtime error raised if attempt to decode beyond cap 3) telemetry tag for "capped_by_runtime".

Priya (eng-runtime): Patch also includes a fallback where if a stream is flagged long-running (>60s without tokens) runtime will abort generation gracefully and mark the request as 429/TOO_LONG.

Maya (oncall): Who's owning follow-up? We need: A) postmortem + customer impact summary B) product decision on hard caps for hosted vs dedicated C) retro on not having runtime upper bound.

Priya (eng-runtime): I'll own the prod change + issue to add integration tests for long-running streaming.

Jared (eng-sre): I'll own infra mitigations: automated eviction policy for runaway sessions, alert for sustained per-key token consumption.

Carlos (customer-success): I'll follow up with affected customers and collect requirements for configurable caps for Dedicated clusters.

Maya (oncall): Handoff to next oncall (Priya) in 20m. Current status: mitigated, customer-impact reduced, mitigations deployed. Logging timeline + artifacts attached to incident page.

Priya (eng-runtime): A quick snippet of the critical logs we saw (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-14T21:12:03Z] E runtime.decode: CUDA error: out of memory (cuCtxAlloc)
[2026-03-14T21:12:03Z] E runtime.decode: attempting to allocate 7.8GB on GPU[0]
[2026-03-14T21:12:03Z] W runtime.session: session id 9b7c... exceeded token threshold (requested=100000)
[2026-03-14T21:12:04Z] F runtime.main: aborting process due to uncaught OOM
```

Priya (eng-runtime): Root cause draft: client sent excessive `max_tokens` with streaming enabled; runtime allowed unbounded streaming generation; decode loop allocation pattern leads to unbounded KV cache growth and eventual CUDA OOM and container crash.

Maya (oncall): Closing notes: Incident severity downgraded to Sev3 now; affected customers notified. We'll file a postmortem and link PR #3456 and infra tickets. Thanks everyone for fast triage. :tada:

Carlos (customer-success): Thanks team. I'll collect customer followups and add to the incident doc.

Priya (eng-runtime): Action items file: https://internal/boards/INC-2026-72-actions - owners assigned.

Maya (oncall): Handoff complete. Leaving channel.

Priya (eng-runtime): I'll draft the postmortem and include mitigations: runtime hard cap, per-key token consumption alert, route-level caps, and a k8s eviction safeguard for long-running streams.

Jared (eng-sre): Also adding a CI test that simulates a client sending a very large `max_tokens` while streaming to ensure defensive behavior can't be bypassed.

(End of thread)
